content: The test image shows a corn ear with extensive mold/rot — white-gray mold with a distinct green patch visible. This is clearly an ear rot. Let me check the relevant reference images.

None of the leaf/stalk diseases (NCLB, Gray leaf spot, Common rust, Tar spot, Stewart's wilt) match — they all affect leaves, not ears. The test image is definitively an ear rot.

**Summary of visual analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Extensive white/gray fluffy mycelial growth covering kernels
- A prominent **bright teal-green patch** in the center of the mold mass
- Degraded/rotted cob tissue underneath

**Key comparison:**
| Class | Color signature | Match? |
|-------|----------------|--------|
| Ear_rots_Trichoderma | White mycelium + **bright teal-green spore masses** | ✅ Strong match |
| Ear_rots_Diplodia | Uniform white/chalky mold, no green | ❌ |
| Ear_rots_Aspergillus | Olive/yellow-green patches on kernels | ❌ (different green hue) |
| Ear_rots_Gibberella | Pink/red mold | ❌ |
| Fusarium | White/pink/salmon mold | ❌ |

The defining feature is the **white mycelium + bright teal-green spore masses** — this is the textbook signature of *Trichoderma* species, which produce characteristic green conidia over white mycelial growth.
